title: Randy Fine
subtitle: Public statements about Gaza, in his own words
summary: A sourced public-record profile of U.S. Representative Randy Fine (Republican, Florida’s 6th District), focused on his posts and broadcast remarks about Gaza. His words are quoted with dates and links. Characterisations by commentators, advocacy groups and journalists are attributed to them. This page asks questions; it is not a finding that any crime has been committed.
scope: A public-record profile of a sitting member of Congress, not a verdict and not a court. A post, a broadcast remark, a commentator’s title and a legal characterisation are different things. Screenshots of posts that could not be located as live records are labelled as unverified here. Inclusion is not a judgment of character.
status_note: Sources reviewed on 13 November 2026, with additional author’s-disclosure sources checked on 14 November 2026. Posts were checked in X’s full archive for the official account @RepFine and the personal account @VoteRandyFine. Automatic captions were obtained for the 3 April 2025 Owen Jones video; because they are machine-generated, Fine’s words are quoted from the original posts and from reporting of a Fox News interview, not from those captions. This page does not find that any statement is a crime, and it does not adopt commentators’ labels as statements of fact.

sections.title: The office and the public record
sections.intro: The biographical facts below are taken from official congressional and Florida legislative sources, cross-checked with Ballotpedia.

paragraphs.text: The official House biography records that Randy Fine was elected to represent Florida’s 6th Congressional District in April 2025 and was sworn in as a member of the U.S. House of Representatives by the Speaker on 2 April 2025. The Office of the Clerk records his party as Republican, his hometown as Melbourne Beach, and his oath date as 2 April 2025. He was assigned to the Committee on Education and the Workforce and the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

sources.locator: biography: election, swearing-in and committee assignments
member profile: Florida 6th, Republican; oath of office 2 April 2025

paragraphs.text: The seat had been vacated by Michael Waltz. Ballotpedia records that Fine won the 1 April 2025 special general election with 110,980 votes (56.7%), ahead of Joshua Weil (Democrat) with 83,580 votes (42.7%). Fine’s official biography states that he earlier served eight years in the Florida House, the statutory maximum, before serving in the Florida Senate and then Congress.

sources.locator: 2025 special general election results; predecessor Michael Waltz
eight years in the Florida House, then the Florida Senate, then Congress

paragraphs.text: The Florida House of Representatives biographical record states that Fine was elected to the House in 2016 and subsequently re-elected. For the 2022–2024 term the same official record lists him as a Republican for District 33, part of Brevard County, and as chair of the Health & Human Services Committee. Ballotpedia, consistent with contemporaneous Florida reporting, records that before the post-2022 maps he represented Florida House District 53. The Florida Senate records that he served as the Republican senator for District 19 (part of Brevard County) and resigned on 31 March 2025.

sources.locator: elected 2016; District 33, 2022–2024 term; biographical information
Florida House 2016–2024, including District 53 and later District 33; Senate District 19
Senator Randy Fine, District 19; resigned 31 March 2025

paragraphs.text: The Florida House biographical information records that he was born on 20 April 1974 in Tucson, Arizona, graduated from Harvard College (A.B., magna cum laude, 1996) and Harvard Business School (M.B.A., with high distinction, 1998), and lists his occupation as businessman. The official congressional biography adds that he founded and ran businesses in retail, technology and hospitality before entering public office, and that colleagues and national Jewish organisations have used the nickname “The Hebrew Hammer” for his work on antisemitism and opposition to terrorism. That nickname also appears in the description of his personal X account. It is recorded here as a self-description and as language used on his official biography, not as a characterisation by this site.

sections.title: The 2026 Republican primary and Dan Bilzerian
sections.intro: Dan Bilzerian did run against Randy Fine in the 2026 Republican primary for Florida’s 6th Congressional District. The figures below are the official, certified results. Bilzerian appeared on the Republican primary ballot, not as an independent candidate.

paragraphs.text: The Florida Division of Elections published official results for the 18 August 2026 Republican primary in Florida’s 6th Congressional District. Randy Fine won and advanced as the Republican nominee, with 51,109 votes (57.6%). Dan Bilzerian, listed as a Republican candidate and not as an independent, finished second, with 16,776 votes (18.9%). Aaron Baker received 12,074 votes (13.6%) and Charles Gambaro 8,716 votes (9.8%). The four-candidate total is 88,675 votes.

sources.locator: Official Results, United States Representative, District 6, Republican primary, 18 August 2026
certified Republican primary tally, 18 August 2026: Fine 51,109 (57.6%), Bilzerian 16,776 (18.9%), Baker 12,074 (13.6%), Gambaro 8,716 (9.8%); total 88,675

paragraphs.text: Ballotpedia’s certified table matches those official totals and records that Fine defeated Bilzerian, Baker and Gambaro. It also lists Manuel Asensio as a Republican who withdrew but remained on the ballot, along with other withdrawn or disqualified Republican candidates who do not appear as vote-getters in the Division of Elections official summary table used here. Some unofficial election-night tallies circulating online included slightly different counts, and in at least one case a small Asensio total; this page uses the official certified figures.

paragraphs.text: Fine was therefore the Republican nominee in the 3 November 2026 general election. This section is confined to the primary challenge from Bilzerian; it does not treat later general-election reporting as a substitute for the official primary record above.

sections.title: The video that prompted this page
sections.intro: The starting point for this profile is a YouTube video sent as a source. The title is the commentator’s. It is quoted as a title, not adopted as a finding.

paragraphs.text: The video is titled “This Genocidal Psycho Just Got Elected To US Congress: ‘May The Streets of Gaza Overflow With Blood’.” YouTube’s oEmbed record and yt-dlp metadata both identify the channel as Owen Jones (https://www.youtube.com/@OwenJonesTalks), the upload date as 3 April 2025, and the duration as 9 minutes 53 seconds. The description reads: “Newly elected Randy Fine shows that you can say literally anything about Palestinians, with no consequences.” Those are Jones’s words and framing, not this site’s.

sources.locator: title, channel, upload date 3 April 2025, duration 593 seconds, description

paragraphs.text: Automatic English captions were downloaded from YouTube’s timed-text service. They are machine-generated speech-to-text, not a human-reviewed transcript, and they contain obvious recognition errors. For that reason this page does not treat the captions as a verbatim record of Fine’s speech. Where Jones quotes or describes particular posts, those posts have been checked against X. Where a post could be located, Fine’s words are quoted from the live (or still-public) post, with a date and URL, below. Where a post could not be located, that is stated.

sections.title: The Fox News interview and the nuclear comparison
sections.intro: In May 2025 Fine gave a Fox News interview after the killing of two Israeli embassy staff in Washington. What he said, how it was reported, and how he answered the reporting are set out separately.

entries.title: What Ynet reported him as saying

paragraphs.text: Ynet, in an article later updated with a correction, reported that Fine was asked whether the Washington shooting changed the calculus on calls for a ceasefire in Gaza. It quoted him as saying: “The only end of the conflict [in Gaza] is complete and total surrender by those who support Muslim terror.” It then quoted him as saying: “In World War II, we didn’t negotiate a surrender with the Nazis. We didn’t negotiate a surrender with the Japanese. We nuked the Japanese twice in order to get unconditional surrender. That needs to be the same here.” And: “The fact of the matter is the Palestinian cause is an evil one. There is something deeply, deeply wrong with this culture, and it needs to be defeated.”

sources.locator: the quoted interview remarks, as published after Ynet’s correction

paragraphs.text: The same Ynet article ends with this correction: “A previous version of this story included a quote suggesting that Rep. Fine called for the use of nuclear weapons in Gaza. The quote has been removed, and the article has been updated to reflect the accurate details. We apologize for any confusion caused as a result of this error.” On 23 May 2025 Fine himself wrote that Ynet had quoted him as saying “we should nuke Gaza,” called that “a fabricated quote, blatant journalistic malpractice,” demanded a formal apology, and said he would be exploring legal action. After Ynet posted a correction, he wrote that it was “not good enough.”

sources.locator: correction at the end of the article

entries.title: How he has explained the remark

paragraphs.text: On 26 May 2025, replying from @VoteRandyFine to a user who had asked whether he had “just call[ed] to nuke Gaza,” Fine wrote a longer explanation: “Neither Fox nor any other legitimate outlet interpreted it as a call to nuke Gaza, which would be a stupid idea on multiple levels (would kill the hostages, fallout drifts into Israel, just to name the two most obvious, and there are many, many, many more).   If you watch the full thing, the statement basically is that Hamas is no different than Nazi Germany or Imperial Japan, and we did whatever was needed to get unconditional surrender.  In the case of Japan, that involved nuking them not once, but twice.  Israel needs to so whatever necessary to obtain the same result -- release of all hostages and unconditional surrender.”

sources.locator: full text, https://x.com/VoteRandyFine/status/1927118679554093369

paragraphs.text: Jewish Insider, in a June 2025 interview, similarly recorded that “contrary to some reports, Fine has denied that he wants to see the territory nuked.” In the same interview it quoted him as arguing that “Palestinians in Gaza are on a level of evil that we saw in Japan and we saw in Germany back in World War II,” and as saying Hamas would not agree to a final surrender “unless the pain is sufficiently great to do that.” Those are Jewish Insider’s quotations of his interview remarks.

sections.title: “Until then, starve away.”
sections.intro: In late July 2025 Fine posted repeatedly about reporting of starvation in Gaza. The posts, and a condemnation from the American Jewish Committee, are set out below.

paragraphs.text: On 22 July 2025, from @RepFine, Fine quote-posted an ABC News post which said: “Fifteen people have died — including four children — from famine and malnutrition in Gaza in the last 24 hours, Hamas-run health ministry says.” Fine wrote: “Release the hostages.     Until then, starve away.    (This is all a lie anyway.  It amazes me that the media continues to regurgitate Muslim terror propaganda.)”

sections.title: How he frames the statements
sections.intro: Fine’s own later posts and interviews are the best evidence of how he says the remarks should be read. They are recorded here as his defence, not as a conclusion of this page.

paragraphs.text: On 12 October 2025, from @RepFine, Fine wrote: “I always find it interesting when I say all terrorists deserve death and Muslims like Cenk hear “kill all the Palestinians.”    Maybe he knows something we don’t?” The remark is his own summary of how he says his words have been heard. It is not independent confirmation that every earlier post was only about Hamas.

sources.locator: https://x.com/RepFine/status/1977364981587775715

paragraphs.text: In a 2 August 2025 post he wrote that “Hamas is pure evil,” that “They’re the ones gouging food prices and hoarding supplies to fund their war machine,” and that “They need to wave the white flag or get wiped out, plain and simple,” ending: “The world should be demanding their unconditional surrender. FREE THE HOSTAGES.” On 3 August 2025 he wrote that “Gaza started a genocidal war whose goal was to kill as many men, women, and children as possible,” and that “if Gazans don’t want more of this, they can release the hostages and surrender.” Those posts put the emphasis on Hamas, hostages and surrender. Other posts quoted above, including “starve away,” “I could care less what happens to Gazans,” and “Destroy it all,” are not, on their face, limited to named members of Hamas. Readers can compare the texts.

sections.title: Responses and calls for censure
sections.intro: Advocacy groups and commentators have used much stronger language than this page will adopt. Their statements are attributed to them.

paragraphs.text: Owen Jones’s video, already cited on this page, is titled “This Genocidal Psycho Just Got Elected To US Congress: “May The Streets of Gaza Overflow With Blood”.” That phrase, “genocidal psycho,” is Jones’s title, not a label of this page. Some users on X have used similar language. On 2 August 2025, in a reply to Fine’s “Yes” post, the account @DiedSuddenly_ (display name Days of Noah) called him a “genocidal maniac.” That is that user’s characterisation, not a finding or a label of this page.

sources.locator: video title, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xCQN25HBbGw
reply of 2 August 2025, 18:17 UTC, https://x.com/DiedSuddenly_/status/1951709063764639891; this page quotes only the characterisation “genocidal maniac”

paragraphs.text: The Council on American-Islamic Relations has, according to Wikipedia’s summary of its statements, labelled Fine an “anti-Muslim extremist” and characterised several of his remarks as “genocidal rhetoric,” including criticism of a post in which he is said to have written “Gaza must be destroyed,” and has called for Congress to condemn and censure him. Those are CAIR’s characterisations. Owen Jones, in the video already cited, argues that the posts amount to “direct and public incitement to commit genocide” under Article III of the 1948 Genocide Convention and under 18 U.S.C. § 1091. That is Jones’s legal argument, not a court finding and not a finding of this page.

sections.title: The question this page will not pretend to decide
sections.intro: Independent Tribunal is not a court. The legal texts are set out so that readers can see what is being asked.

paragraphs.text: Article III of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide lists, among the acts that “shall be punishable,” “(c) Direct and public incitement to commit genocide.” The United States has implemented related offences in federal criminal law, including 18 U.S.C. § 1091, which addresses genocide and, in that setting, direct and public incitement. Those texts exist independently of this page.

sources.locator: Article III(c)

paragraphs.text: The questions worth asking, and which this page does not answer as a finding, include these. Do these statements amount to direct and public incitement to genocide under Article III(c), or to advocacy of collective punishment? Do they remain, as Fine says, calls for the defeat of Hamas and for unconditional surrender, directed at a terrorist organisation and not at a civilian population? A post that uses “Gazans” or “Palestinian” without naming Hamas is not automatically a legal conclusion either way. Suspicion is not proof. A commentator’s title is not a verdict. Independent Tribunal is an independent public-interest research and accountability initiative, not a court with coercive or judicial powers.

sources.locator: the text of Article III(c), against which the question is asked
Fine’s stated defence: unconditional surrender, not a call to nuke Gaza

sections.title: Randy Fine vs Dan Bilzerian in primaries

group.title: Randy Fine vs Dan Bilzerian in primaries

sections.intro: This is a first-person statement by Mars Robertson, the author of IndependentTribunal.org, about his position in the 2026 Republican primary between Randy Fine and Dan Bilzerian, and a short related aside about another campaign. It is his own account, clearly marked as such, and not a finding of this page.

entries.title: A statement in the author’s own name

paragraphs.text: Randy Fine was the reason I conditionally and strategically supported Bilzerian’s primary challenge. I was doing strategic support of a candidate with 28.5 million followers to boost my career. In that race I supported Dan Bilzerian’s campaign on a provisional and temporary basis. On 10 November 2026 I wrote, from @MarsitaTheUltra: “I support independent candidates, in principle. @DanBilzerian @ElectBilzerian was totally unserious about the campaign, 28.5M followers on Insta and not a single post... Totally unserious. My support to his campaign was provisional and temporary.” The post names Bilzerian and the campaign account @ElectBilzerian. Official election records, set out above, show that Bilzerian ran as a Republican in the 18 August 2026 primary, not as an independent candidate. My post also stated a general principle of supporting independent candidates. This is my own statement, not a finding of this page.

That support was strategic and conditional. It was directed at a candidate with a large Instagram platform — the post gives the figure as 28.5 million followers — and at the possibility of reaching that audience. In politics and diplomacy, one may support or withhold support strategically, based on overarching objectives. An artist looking for an audience is a commonplace example. Support of that kind is not an endorsement of every view a candidate holds. I do not support Nazis. I refuse to call myself, or be labelled, a Nazi supporter.

I was made aware of the Nazi insignia. At the time I remained consistent with my strategy. In a further post the same day, at 16:04:55 UTC on 10 November 2026, I wrote the words quoted below. Official records still show that Bilzerian was a Republican primary candidate. The word “independent” in that post is mine; it does not change the ballot line. I’m extra cautious. If more Nazi stuff appears I will re-evaluate. That is my position now, not a finding of this page about any person.

I’m 100% honest: I had my own agendas. I do not support Nazis, and I support the “genocidal psycho” even less. “Genocidal psycho” is Owen Jones’s phrase, used as the title of his 3 April 2025 YouTube video about Fine; it is not a label of this page. As of 14 November 2026, YouTube’s structured data on Jones’s channel page, @OwenJonesTalks, listed 896,000 subscribers (some labels on the same page showed 895k). A journalist with roughly 896,000 YouTube subscribers uses that label openly in a published video title.

The YouTube listing for this video, on the channel Mars Robertson (genesis.re) at @genesisdotre, is titled “Why do I support Bilzerian?” YouTube’s video page lists the upload date as 28 May 2026, 17:50 Pacific Daylight Time (29 May 2026, 00:50 UTC) and the duration as 4 minutes 39 seconds. The published description reads: “Follow me on Twitter: https://x.com/MarsitaTheUltra/status/2060160929245909437” and “Clips from: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=llYEEX2lws8”. This page records that listing. It does not treat the video or those clips as a transcript, and it does not describe footage that has not been independently verified here. The video is embedded below, with a direct link if the embed does not load.

On 10 November 2026 at 16:04:55 UTC I posted the following from @MarsitaTheUltra, in the same thread as the earlier support post. The post as retrieved included a photograph, which is not reproduced here. Official records, set out above, show that Bilzerian ran as a Republican in the primary, not as an independent.
@olamtrade180 @DanBilzerian @LauraLoomer @RepFine @Cyntaxed007 @RepThomasMassie @u_independents @owenjonesjourno @ElectBilzerian Which planet are you on?
Strategic support for independent candidate ≠ supporting a nazi.
At the time of issuing initial support I was informed about nazi insignia. Bearing in mind all the circumstances I remained consistent (could be a cognitive bias) towards an independent

entries.title: A related aside: the author’s view of the Green Party motion

paragraphs.text: This short aside is a related lesson I draw from another campaign; it is not part of the Florida primary record. I appreciate the lessons from the “Zionism is racism” motion at the Green Party of England and Wales annual conference in Brighton in October 2026. BBC News reported that members passed the motion on Sunday 4 October 2026 by 1,022 votes to 813, and that Zack Polanski, the party’s leader, left the conference before the vote to campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election. He was the Green candidate in that by-election, held on 8 October 2026; he was not the Green candidate in Holborn and St Pancras at the 4 July 2024 general election, when David Stansell stood for the party. Official UK Parliament results show that Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali won the by-election with 12,292 votes (45.2%) and that Polanski came second with 8,928 votes (32.8%), on a turnout of 38.6%. It is my own view, not a finding established by those sources, that the motion derailed his bid to become MP for the seat.

paragraphs.text: In my own view, which is not a finding of this page, that motion was a clusterfuck of epic proportions. Rather than focus on a historic breakthrough, on something majestic, they chose to focus on something shockingly bad. I am very not compliant, very not complicit.

paragraphs.text: A panel in the satire graphic below refers to a September 2025 dispute, reported by BBC News, over a Your Party membership launch. On 18 September 2025 the BBC reported that Jeremy Corbyn described an email promoting a membership portal as “unauthorised,” and that Zarah Sultana said she had launched the portal after being sidelined, and that that week’s emails did not have the “dual authorisation of both myself and Jeremy,” which, she said, “was the agreement made at the start of this process.” Those are the parties’ own characterisations as reported by the BBC, not findings of this page.

sources.locator: Sam Francis, 18 September 2025: Corbyn called the email “unauthorised”; Sultana said the week’s emails lacked the agreed dual authorisation
